subject: Air-gapped artifact provenance & emergency rollback flow
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Acme Corp SecOps <secops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped artifact provenance & emergency rollback flow

Team / Samira,

Following our onboarding review last week, I sketched a concise flow for how we plan to deliver signed runtime images and emergency rollback artifacts into Acme's air-gapped environment. Goal: minimal manual steps for on-prem infra while preserving an auditable chain-of-custody and a fast emergency patch/rollback path.

High-level proposal (attached: airgap-manifest-schema-v1.json, physical-media-coc-form.pdf, image-signing-checklist.md):

1) Build & sign (Redwood CI/CD):
   - Images are produced in the build farm; each image has a monotonic build id and content hash (sha256).
   - Sign the image manifest with our offline HSM key (PKCS#11-backed); produce both a detached signature and a signed manifest.json containing: build_id, model_version, container_digest, signing_key_id, tlog_entry_id.

2) Packaging to removable media:
   - The delivery bundle contains: signed-manifest.json, image.tar.gz (or OCI tar), verify.sh, install-manifest.yml, and a short readme.
   - Every media shipment is paired with a filled chain-of-custody (CoC) PDF (physical-media-coc-form.pdf) signed by the shipping custodian.

3) Customer ingestion & verification (on Acme side):
   - Verify signature via our public signing cert (we will provide pinned cert and fingerprint in advance).
   - Run included test vectors (test-vector-suite.tar.gz) in an isolated verification environment before install.

4) Rollback & emergency patch channel:
   - We maintain a signed rollback bundle (previous N images) on an offline-accessible S3 snapshot and as sealed removable media for certified emergencies.
   - Escalation trigger: security-critical CVE, or customer-detected correctness regression.
   - Escalation path: Acme raises a SecOps ticket + Redwood PS leads a runbook with SLA timelines (we propose 4 hours to validated rollback artifact).

Open questions for the group:
- Priyom: does the manifest/signature format satisfy typical audit requirements (we want minimal additional attestation from Acme side)?
- Dev: can the verify.sh be reduced to a single step for customers and still cover all checks (hash, sig, tlog proof)?
- Vivek: commercial ask — do we need a contractual clause for physical-media handling / custodian transfer liability?

Samira — please confirm the verification constraints your infra team requires (e.g., FIPS-only verification tools, endpoint restrictions for checksum tools). I attached the schema and a checklist for review.

Next steps: if no major blockers, I'll schedule a short run-through call and a test shipment to your staging rack next Wednesday.

Thanks,

-- 
Marissa Cole
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Aug 17, 2027 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com> wrote:
> Team / Samira,
>
> Following our onboarding review last week, I sketched a concise flow for how we plan to deliver signed runtime images and emergency rollback artifacts into Acme's air-gapped environment.

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and pragmatic. A few clarifications from implementability perspective:

- verify.sh: propose a tiny shim that calls three binaries from our distro: rwinf-verify (signature + tlog proof), rwinf-checksum (sha256 validation), and rwinf-sig-publish (optional: publishes successful verification to an internal attestation store if connected). If Acme is fully offline, the script will skip attestation publish but still emit a signed verification receipt they can store.

- TLog: we currently mirror SignedEntries to an offline Transparency Log snapshot (tlog-snapshot.tar) that we include in the media when requested. That lets customers verify inclusion proofs without external network calls.

- Test vectors: will produce a lightweight smoke test that exercises model startup, KV cache warmup, and a deterministic output assertion to validate integrity. Running time: ~6 minutes on a modest host.

I'll attach a draft verify.sh and the proposed CLI flags (small file). Also flag for Priyom: if we include long-lived cert fingerprints in the manifest, we must have a rotation policy documented.

- Dev

-- 
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[attachment: verify-shim-v1.sh (executable script)]

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Acme Corp SecOps <secops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped artifact provenance & emergency rollback flow

Thanks — this direction helps. A few notes from Acme SecOps requirements: 

1) FIPS-validated crypto: our compliance team requires use of FIPS-validated modules for signature verification. Can rwinf-verify be built against our FIPS toolchain or provide a compatibility layer?
2) Chain-of-custody: the CoC PDF you included looks fine, but for corporate shipping we need explicit time-stamped notarization on shipper signature (we use our carrier partner). Can Redwood accept a notarized CoC or only the plain signed PDF?
3) Rollback SLA: 4 hours to validated artifact is acceptable if Redwood can pre-provision a signed rollback bundle in our shared vault (offline snapshot + physical media). Otherwise 24 hours is our expectation.

Also, for auditing we'll need a short test matrix of verification steps we can include in our compliance packet (I saw the test vectors attached — can you provide pass/fail expected outputs?).

If you can address FIPS and the notarized CoC, we can greenlight the test shipment to staging next Wednesday.

— Samira
Samira Khan
Senior Manager, Infrastructure Security
Acme Corp
(samira.khan@acme-corp.com)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-corp.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped artifact provenance & emergency rollback flow

Samira — thanks, great questions. Quick answers and next actions: 

- FIPS: Priyom and I confirmed yesterday that the rwinf-verify shim can be compiled with a FIPS-approved crypto provider; Priyom will own a small compatibility matrix and provide static builds for your staging host. (action: Priyom to deliver by EOD Friday).

- Notarized CoC: we can accept a notarized CoC. Our shipping vendor will include a notarization stamp when requested; we will also retain scanned notarized receipts in our compliance folder and include a redacted copy in the Drive link (see related_links).

- Rollback SLA: we can commit to a 4-hour validated artifact response if Acme agrees to: (a) pre-provision an encrypted vault slice we can write rollback bundles to, or (b) accept a staged sealed media held by the carrier partner and a signed manifest in your vault. If neither option is possible, fallback 24-hour SLA applies. We should capture the chosen option in the SOW.

- Test vectors: Dev will attach expected outputs; I'll also produce a 1-page checklist for your auditors (pass/fail) and include it in the final shipment.

Plan: Priyom (security) and Dev (solutions) — please build the FIPS static binary and the verification receipt flow. Samira — if you confirm notarized CoC and one of the rollback options above, we'll schedule the staging shipment for Wed 2027-08-25 09:00 local.

Thanks all — will follow-up with updated artifacts and a short runbook for the staging run.

-- 
Marissa Cole
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
